findings.title: Unsubscribe mutates notification state on a plain GET request
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action is exposed via GET (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) and immediately changes the user's `notification_level` in the database before rendering. GET requests are issued without user intent by mail-client link prefetchers, virus scanners (e.g. Outlook SafeLinks), and browser prerendering, and they carry no CSRF protection. Any such automated fetch of the unsubscribe URL will silently mute/change the user's topic subscription. Unsubscribe-via-GET should either require a POST confirmation or at minimum not apply the state change until the user confirms on the rendered page.

findings.title: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, causing a 500 on unsubscribe
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is not guaranteed to exist. Users can receive notification emails without ever having a topic_users row for the topic (e.g. mailing-list mode subscribers, or users notified via category watching where the row was never created). In that case `tu.notification_level` on line 107 raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link from the email returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` which creates the row when missing.

findings.title: Direct save bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: The action mutates `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of `TopicUser.change`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not set, and no `notification_level_change` message is published on MessageBus, so any open browser tabs of that user keep showing the old notification state and reporting that relies on the changed-at/reason fields is wrong. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` for consistency with every other code path that changes notification levels.

findings.title: ensure_logged_in blocks the email unsubscribe flow for logged-out users
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is added to the `ensure_logged_in` filter list. The feature's entry point is a link in a notification email, and recipients frequently are not logged in (mobile mail clients, different browser). Those users are bounced to the login page and, even after logging in, are not taken back to the unsubscribe URL, so the one-click unsubscribe silently fails for exactly the audience it targets. Consider a signed token in the unsubscribe URL (like the existing digest unsubscribe key) instead of requiring a session.

findings.title: Watching/tracking users are demoted to 'regular', still receiving notifications
findings.body: The logic sets the level to `regular` when it is currently above regular, and only mutes when it is regular or below. A user watching a topic (the most common reason for getting email) who clicks 'stop receiving notifications about this topic' is moved to regular, under which they still receive reply/mention notifications. The email copy ('To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here') and the page text ('You will stop receiving notifications') then claim the opposite of what happened.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url} but not all callers pass it
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` in `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` is invoked for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`; any current or future caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without passing `unsubscribe_url` (e.g. plugins, or the spec's own builder which previously only used `add_unsubscribe_link: true`) will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and the email will fail to send. Either make the per-topic sentence conditional on the URL being present or guard against the missing key.

findings.title: No controller/request specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The PR adds a state-changing endpoint (`topics#unsubscribe`), new routes, and a mailer link, but the only spec change is adding an `unsubscribe_url` option to an existing message-builder test. There is no coverage for the redirect-on-slug-mismatch branch, the level-downgrade/mute logic, the nil TopicUser case, or the requirement that the user be logged in — all of which contain bugs noted above.
